extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, media scholars, and the informed public
extracted.subtask_description: A set of guiding principles and professional standards for practicing, evaluating, and expecting journalism; focuses on ethics, verification, independence, public service, and the role of news in a democratic society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal conscience as foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should adhere to a personal conscience, which provides a solid foundation for all other principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors propose that several guiding principles should define both journalism and our expectations of those who provide it. The most important, they suggest, is that journalists have an obligation to personal conscience. Adhering to that principle can provide a solid foundation for all of the others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose: inform citizens for self-governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose of journalism is to provide citizens with the information they need to be free and self-governing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism exists to give citizens the information necessary to participate in democratic life and to make informed choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: First obligation: the truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism's first obligation is to the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truth is the paramount duty; reporting should aim at accuracy and honesty above other considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: First loyalty: to citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism's first loyalty is to citizens rather than to advertisers, owners, special interests, or the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters and news organizations should place the needs and rights of the public before other loyalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline of verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The essence of journalism is a discipline of verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic practice should emphasize rigorous fact-checking and verification procedures as central to producing reliable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain independence from those covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must maintain an independence from those they cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest and relationships that compromise impartiality; independence is essential to credible reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve as independent monitors of power
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must serve as independent monitors of power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press should hold public and private power to account by investigating and reporting abuses and decisions that affect the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a forum for public criticism and comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism must provide a forum for public criticism and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News outlets should facilitate public discourse, allowing diverse voices, debate, and feedback to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the significant interesting and relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must make the significant interesting and relevant to their audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should connect important issues to readers' or viewers' lives, using storytelling and presentation that engage without sacrificing substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep news in proportion and make it comprehensive
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should keep the news in proportion and make coverage comprehensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensationalism and provide context so that audiences understand the relative importance of events and issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist corporate pressures and entertainment bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and news organizations should resist corporate ownership pressures that favor entertainment over informing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review notes increasing concentration of ownership and corporate priorities that push publications and television programs to become more entertaining at the expense of informing (example: Time and Newsweek increasingly running the same cover story as People). Journalists should guard against these pressures to preserve news quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act as gatekeepers amid information overload
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism must help audiences navigate an expanding and noisy media environment by providing reliable, substantive information amid abundant unverified content online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Internet opens unprecedented fields of expression, it also enables anyone to publish unsubstantiated material. The danger is countless distracting sources and very few reliable outlets; relying on aggressive, reliable journalism can help audiences find trustworthy information rather than being 'swamped by the junk.'
